stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U ≥ T > X < P ≤ Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: U < Q. II: T ≤ X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain T > Q ≤ S < W < Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: T ≤ S. II: S = W.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X > W < U ≥ Q > P, decide which conclusions follow. I: X > W. II: W > U.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S = Q < T ≥ P < R, decide which conclusions follow. I: T ≤ P. II: S < Q.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain P > Z < X < Q ≤ R, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z > X. II: Z ≤ X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Statements: Some bakers are readers. Some readers are artists. Conclusions: I. Some bakers are artists. II. All artists are bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some poets are workers. All workers are pilots. Conclusions: I. Some poets are pilots. II. All poets are pilots. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Statements: No bakers are painters. Some painters are poets. Conclusions: I. Some poets are not bakers. II. No poets are bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Statements: All readers are pilots. No pilots are runners. Conclusions: I. No readers are runners. II. Some readers are runners. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Statements: Some farmers are drivers. No drivers are poets. Conclusions: I. Some farmers are not poets. II. All farmers are poets. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The A∩B members cannot be C.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 60 km north, then 48 km east, then 12 km south and finally 12 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net north = 48 km and east = 36 km. Distance = √(48²+36²) = 60 km.

questions.stem: Kiran moves 12 km north, 72 km east, 36 km south and 12 km west. In which direction is Kiran from the start?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 108 km north, 48 km east, 60 km south and 12 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Total path length = 108+48+60+12=228 km (not displacement).
